title: Specification Surfaces for Incremental Predictive Performance: analysis code, pre-registrations, derived results, a verification harness and the fieldvalue package
description:
Analysis code, three pre-registrations, derived result files, figures, a verification harness and a Python package for the study Specification Surfaces for Incremental Predictive Performance: Estimation, Uncertainty, and Multi-Log Evaluation.

The problem. What a recorded field is worth to a prediction is reported as one number. That number is a functional of design choices — the baseline it is measured against, the learner, the encoding, the target, the temporal split, the field's availability at the decision time, the register's quality, the metric and the operating point — which are rarely stated. The study defines the quantity as a specification surface over a declared, enumerable design space and supplies four objects for estimating and reporting one.

The four objects. (1) An exact functional-ANOVA (Sobol) decomposition of the surface's variance across design axes. (2) Simultaneous max-t confidence bands from a moving-block bootstrap that refits the entire pipeline — encoders, frequency tables, target encodings, register rankings, calibrators — inside every draw. (3) Resolution regions (uniformly beneficial, conditionally beneficial, sign-changing, unresolved) with a scalar robustness index. (4) Specification regret, which measures what conventional one-number reporting gets wrong.

What the evidence says. Over 19 log-target pairs from 13 public event logs across 6 domains, varying the baseline alone moves the increment by 0.073 AUC at the median pair and 0.252 at the widest. No single axis dominates the disagreement between analysts: the largest first-order sensitivity index at the median pair is 28.7%, and interactions between axes carry a median 56.0%. A conventional one-number report misstates the sign of the increment for a median 32.8% of the other admissible specifications, and the rate exceeds 10% on 18 of the 19 pairs.

The case study. A configuration management database on a public log of 46,606 bank incidents on the registered cohort, evaluated on a named decision. Its answer turns on which of two decision times the analyst occupies, because a knowledge-article reference is written in between; the archive reports both surfaces and a curve of the increment against the share of references assumed to be written after the fact, rather than choosing.

Pre-registrations. PROTOCOL.md fixes the corpus, the targets, the role-assignment rules, the exclusion codes, the estimator and the seed. AUDIT-PROTOCOL-2.md fixes the frame, the sampling design, the two-stratum adjudication and the estimators for a machine-assisted prevalence pilot of reporting practice. PREDICTION.md freezes a rule and its threshold before either held-out log was downloaded. Each was committed alone, before any result it governs; git log --stat is the evidence.

One source of truth for every number. The manuscript contains no numeric literal. Every number is a macro in paper/numbers.tex, generated by scripts/make_numbers.py from results/*.csv, and every data table is generated too. A number therefore cannot disagree between the abstract, a table and the conclusion: there is one of it. scripts/verify_numbers.py re-derives each macro from its source with independent code; scripts/texlint.py fails the build if a numeric literal appears in the prose, if the abstract exceeds 200 words, if there are more than six keywords, if a highlight exceeds 85 characters or misstates its own length, or if a required statement is missing.

The package. fieldvalue/ computes a surface and refuses by design to emit a single number, and now also implements the four reporting objects as functions of a surface: decompose, regions, robustness and regret. 108 tests.

What is included. Every analysis script, every derived results/*.csv, the figure generators, the manuscript source and its generated parts, an environment locked by artefact hash, a container that pins BLAS thread counts, the pilot's adjudications with a free-text reason for every judgement, a referee log, and a point-by-point response to the referee report that this version answers.

What is not included. No row of any dataset, and no full text of any audited paper. Every dataset is public and is cited by persistent identifier; the pilot's full texts and the evidence dossiers built from them are regenerated from each work's own open-access location by scripts/s06_audit2.py.

What the harness does not do. It guards numbers thoroughly and prose only where a guard was written by hand. The correction register in the manuscript's Appendix C groups the author's own errors by class rather than listing them as incidents, and the largest class is sentences in which every printed number was correct and the relation asserted between them was not. The generated-macro discipline makes one sub-class of that structurally impossible; it does not make the rest impossible.
notes: Round nineteen. This release accompanies a manuscript that replaces an earlier one, 'Four Choices Behind One Number: Reporting the Incremental Value of a Recorded Field', which a referee for Information Systems recommended rejecting as submitted. The earlier manuscript is retained in the archive; submission/response_to_referee.md answers the ten major comments one by one, and every claim of the earlier version that this one withdraws is recorded as a correction in the new manuscript's Appendix C. Round twenty answers a second, developmental review: three surfaces distinguished and audited, whole-surface simultaneous bands with a multiplier-bootstrap critical value, an orthogonal variance decomposition under declared measures, regret computed inside one instrument at a time and evaluated out of sample, plus-one bootstrap p-values, training-only calibration before every decision curve, and a corrected rank-invariance proposition with a counterexample to the previous statement. Round twenty-five closes the two open methodological items: scripts/s41_bandcoverage.py measures the max-t band's family-wise coverage against a known answer over families matched to this corpus, and finds that the band does not attain its nominal level anywhere in this corpus's configuration; and the coverage-calibration plane is widened in n from three training sizes to eleven, which shows that K/n alone does not determine the factor and that past a crossing in n the basic interval stops containing its own point estimate, so the factor is undefined there. Round 25 of REFEREE-LOG.md records both, together with four defects found while closing them.
